newsitem.title: FRANCE: SOCCER-MARSEILLE RESTORE PRIDE BY BEATING MONACO.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-MARSEILLE RESTORE PRIDE BY BEATING MONACO.

text.p: Troubled Marseille restored some pride with an impressive 3-1 win over title-chasing Monaco in the French soccer league on Tuesday.
The former European champions, who had taken only one point from their last five games, bounced back in style to the delight of their fans packing the Velodrome stadium.
Marseille, without a goal for 393 minutes, went ahead after just 70 seconds thanks to striker Xavier Gravelaine, set up by a brilliant pass from midfielder Ludovic Asuar.
Captain Jean-Philippe Durand, who came back only recently after a long injury break, scored his side's second goal with a shot from close range in the 12th minute.
Marseille sustained their attacks, making it 3-0 after 30 minutes with a superb acrobatic volley from midfielder Eric Roy.
Monaco, beaten only twice in their previous 15 matches, reduced the arrears with two minutes remaining through a penalty by Brazilian Anderson.
"I have to congratulate my players for their courage," said Marseille trainer Gerard Gili, who would probably have been sacked had Marseille lost.
"The most important thing for us was to win. As for my future, we'll talk about it later."
Marseille climb two places to 12th in the 20-team division while Monaco stay second but are now under pressure from Auxerre.
The third-placed French champions, one point behind Monaco, are home to Metz on Wednesday while leaders Paris St Germain travel to Nice.
